ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities in the fields of science and engineering. Through its strategic initiative, ETH Zurich │ Space is systematically expanding its activities in space research and technology. A unique environment for innovation is being created through the recruitment of high-calibre researchers of international standing and the expansion of collaborations with leading partners from academia, space agencies and industry.
Within the Vice-Presidency for Knowledge Transfer and Corporate Relations, the Research Contracts Group supports researchers in ensuring that their projects with national and international partners are built on a solid legal foundation.
To strengthen our team, we are seeking, with immediate effect or by agreement, a committed, solution-oriented and strong negotiator to take on the role of Legal Counsel for ETH Zurich │ Space.
Job description

s.h: Your role at the interface between space research and law
s.t:
In this role, you will be the key legal point of contact for the research activities of ETH Zurich │ Space and ETH Swiss GeoLab. You will be part of a strong team of around 20 legal professionals in the Research Contracts Group, where you will benefit from their broad expertise and mutual exchange of ideas.

Your personal focus will be on independently managing the space-related portfolio.

Against the backdrop of a steadily growing number of collaborations, you will facilitate and promote the conclusion of contracts between ETH researchers and space-related organisations – ranging from industrial companies and start-ups to international space agencies, as well as academic and public institutions.

You will advise researchers and management on the drafting and negotiation of complex research contracts and help to ensure that innovative research projects are implemented in a legally sound and efficient manner.

This encompasses both traditional space technologies (e.g. hardware) and Earth observation, the processing of geo-information and the use of space data on Earth. In doing so, you also act as a bridge to Swiss stakeholders in government bodies and the business sector.
You will support scientists with their projects from the initial idea for collaboration right through to the conclusion of a contract and lay the legal foundations for world-class international research in a highly dynamic environment.

· You will independently review, draft and negotiate complex national and international research and development contracts, in particular Research Collaboration Agreements, Consortium Agreements, Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs) and other research and cooperation agreements.
· You will manage projects with international space agencies, research institutions and industry partners, particularly within the context of the European Space Agency (ESA), NASA, the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) and other international space and research partners.
· You will advise researchers and project managers on legal issues relating to international research collaborations, intellectual property, liability matters and other contractual risks.
· You will provide support on matters relating to export controls and dual-use goods, working closely with the relevant compliance units at ETH Zurich.
· You will provide proactive and solution-oriented advice to researchers and project managers throughout the entire project lifecycle – from project initiation to successful completion.
· You will further develop contract templates, guidelines and standard processes for the efficient and legally compliant management of space and research projects.
· You will work closely with ETH transfer, compliance units and other internal and external stakeholders.
· You will make a significant contribution to ensuring that international research collaborations are legally sound, whilst at the same time safeguarding the research community’s ability to act.
Profile
We are looking for someone who can quickly grasp complex issues, develop pragmatic solutions and takes pleasure in supporting researchers in a world-class international research environment.
· Education: You hold a university degree in law (or equivalent legal qualification) combined with a strong understanding of technical contexts.
· Experience: You have at least 5 years’ relevant professional experience in international contract law or research management – ideally gained in an international organisation, a company in the tech/space sector, a space-related authority or at a university. Experience with contracts from space agencies (e.g. ESA) or space companies is a strong advantage.
· Expertise: You have in-depth knowledge of Swiss and international contract law. Experience in intellectual property law, technology transfer or research law is an advantage.
· Space law: Knowledge of international space law, regulatory issues relating to the space sector, and the science policy context of international research collaborations would be an advantage.
· Export control & regulation: Experience in export control law (particularly ITAR/EAR), in dealing with dual-use goods or in comparable regulatory environments is particularly welcome. Knowledge of ESA or NASA-related regulatory frameworks is an additional advantage.
· Skills: You possess excellent analytical and conceptual skills, strong negotiation skills, and the ability to address legal risks in a pragmatic and solution-oriented manner.
· Languages: You communicate and negotiate fluently in German and English (both spoken and written). Business-level English is essential.
· Mindset & working style: You are characterised by a strong service orientation and a pragmatic, solution-oriented approach to your work. You are a talented communicator and are confident in your interactions with researchers, industry representatives and regulatory authorities.
By drafting clear and balanced contractual provisions, you lay the foundations for successful international collaborations. You can manage a demanding portfolio independently and conduct complex contract negotiations efficiently and in a goal-oriented manner.
If, in addition, you have an interest in the space sector, cutting-edge technology and international research collaborations, and are passionate about scientific innovation, you are ideally suited for this role.

As the day-to-day owner of the privacy compliance program, you will be responsible for developing AI solutions for operating and maturing the controls that keep Databricks compliant, and serve as a trusted advisor to business partners across the company.
You will be agile, highly organized, and have the skills, drive, and flexibility to build and scale a program at a leading technology company, addressing cutting-edge legal issues and organizational challenges. A successful candidate will be an AI proficient builder, resourceful self-starter, comfortable working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, and excellent at building strong relationships and driving cross-functional execution.
The impact you will have
Program Leadership: Own day-to-day operation of the Databricks privacy compliance program. Define priorities, establish and track program metrics and KPIs, and report on program health, risks, and maturity.
Business and Legal Judgment: Exercise practical judgment about when to approve, approve with conditions, decline, or escalate.
Privacy Program Compliance: Lead the further development, implementation, and continuous improvement of core program components — data subject rights requests, data inventory and data mapping (ROPA), records of processing, privacy by design, and the policies and processes that make the program run. Operate and improve the effectiveness of critical privacy compliance workflows.
End-to-End Privacy by Design & Risk Assessments: Develop privacy review processes for the full data and product lifecycle — from ideation to end of life. Improve.
Contract Negotiation and Transactions: Draft and update form agreements, and counsel on and negotiate data protection provisions in commercial contracts, including data processing addendums (DPAs), standard contractual clauses (SCCs), and related data-transfer instruments.
Regulatory Analysis & Engagement: Monitor, research, and evaluate the applicability and impact of global privacy and AI laws, legislation, and regulatory guidance on new business initiatives. Support responses to regulator inquiries, audits, and enforcement developments.
Policy Development: Develop, review, and maintain privacy policies, standards, notices, and procedures to align with legal requirements and best practices.
Process Improvement: Contribute to developing and refining the processes that improve the privacy function, and partner with your stakeholders to build scalable process improvements as the business grows.
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Legal Partnership: Build deep cross-functional relationships and collaborate with other legal leaders in commercial, go-to-market, compliance, corporate, and public affairs on privacy issues. Own the privacy training and awareness program, delivering strategic and timely enablement to keep the organization compliant.
Incident Response: Advise on privacy and cybersecurity issues as a member of incident response teams, including breach assessment, notification analysis, and remediation, in partnership with the Legal Product team and Security.
Team Contribution: Provide general legal support on a flexible, as-needed basis with respect to other areas of the business, and contribute as a team player to further the legal department's reputation as an effective, respected, and valued resource within the company.
What we look for
7+ years of relevant legal experience at a top law firm and/or in-house (a combination of both is a plus), with 5+ years focused on privacy and demonstrated experience building, operating, or leading a privacy compliance program (not solely advisory work)
Deep, current knowledge of global privacy frameworks, including the GDPR/UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA and the growing patchwork of U.S. state comprehensive privacy laws, and familiarity with cross-border data transfer mechanisms (SCCs, IDTA, adequacy, EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework)
Working knowledge of the operational building blocks of a privacy program — DPIAs/PIAs, ROPA and data mapping, data subject rights processes, privacy by design, and vendor/third-party risk management
Capacity to be a generalist and learn new areas of law and legal skills quickly as the business evolves
Deep understanding of cloud and software technology, and a strong desire to work on legal issues in these areas
Experience working for a company offering platform services to business customers is a plus
Familiarity with privacy management tooling (e.g., OneTrust or comparable) is a plus
J.D. from a top-tier law school
State bar membership required, in good standing
One or more privacy certifications (e.g., CIPP/E, CIPP/US, CIPM, CIPT, FIP) preferred; CIPM is particularly valued for a program-leadership role

You can set direction for a program and drive it to execution — prioritizing and managing time and client expectations in the face of competing demands, often without direct guidance, as we scale our rapidly expanding business.
You exercise good judgment in raising issues, assessing risk, and providing concise, actionable, business-focused legal advice and counsel.
You build strong, deep working relationships with internal stakeholders across multiple geographies and functions, and are comfortable working with distributed teams.
You are a self-starter who operates independently and interacts confidently with senior management, influencing without authority.
You have a strong work ethic, excellent organizational skills, and the ability to manage many cross-functional projects simultaneously with minimal supervision.
You have outstanding written and verbal communication skills, and can make complex privacy and regulatory concepts clear to both legal and non-legal audiences, including executives.

# Legal Counsel / Contracts Specialist for ETH Zurich | Space #
#### 100%, Zurich, permanent ####
print Drucken
ETH Zurich is one of the world-s leading universities in the fields of science and engineering. Through its strategic initiative, **ETH Zurich - Space** is systematically expanding its activities in space research and technology. A unique environment for innovation is being created through the recruitment of high-calibre researchers of international standing and the expansion of collaborations with leading partners from academia, space agencies and industry.
Within the Vice-Presidency for Knowledge Transfer and Corporate Relations, the Research Contracts Group supports researchers in ensuring that their projects with national and international partners are built on a solid legal foundation.
To strengthen our team, we are seeking, with immediate effect or by agreement, a committed, solution-oriented and strong negotiator to take on the role of Legal Counsel for ETH Zurich - Space.
## Job description ##

s.h: **Your role at the interface between space research and law**
s.t:
In this role, you will be the key legal point of contact for the research activities of ETH Zurich - Space and ETH Swiss GeoLab. You will be part of a strong team of around 20 legal professionals in the Research Contracts Group, where you will benefit from their broad expertise and mutual exchange of ideas.

Your personal focus will be on independently managing the space-related portfolio.

Against the backdrop of a steadily growing number of collaborations, you will facilitate and promote the conclusion of contracts between ETH researchers and space-related organisations - ranging from industrial companies and start-ups to international space agencies, as well as academic and public institutions.

You will advise researchers and management on the drafting and negotiation of complex research contracts and help to ensure that innovative research projects are implemented in a legally sound and efficient manner.

This encompasses both traditional space technologies (e.g. hardware) and Earth observation, the processing of geo-information and the use of space data on Earth. In doing so, you also act as a bridge to Swiss stakeholders in government bodies and the business sector.
You will support scientists with their projects from the initial idea for collaboration right through to the conclusion of a contract and lay the legal foundations for world-class international research in a highly dynamic environment.

* You will independently review, draft and negotiate complex national and international research and development contracts, in particular Research Collaboration Agreements, Consortium Agreements, Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs) and other research and cooperation agreements.
* You will manage projects with international space agencies, research institutions and industry partners, particularly within the context of the European Space Agency (ESA), NASA, the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) and other international space and research partners.
* You will advise researchers and project managers on legal issues relating to international research collaborations, intellectual property, liability matters and other contractual risks.
* You will provide support on matters relating to export controls and dual-use goods, working closely with the relevant compliance units at ETH Zurich.
* You will provide proactive and solution-oriented advice to researchers and project managers throughout the entire project lifecycle - from project initiation to successful completion.
* You will further develop contract templates, guidelines and standard processes for the efficient and legally compliant management of space and research projects.
* You will work closely with ETH transfer, compliance units and other internal and external stakeholders.
* You will make a significant contribution to ensuring that international research collaborations are legally sound, whilst at the same time safeguarding the research community-s ability to act.
## Profile ##
We are looking for someone who can quickly grasp complex issues, develop pragmatic solutions and takes pleasure in supporting researchers in a world-class international research environment.
* **Education:** You hold a university degree in law (or equivalent legal qualification) combined with a strong understanding of technical contexts.
* **Experience:** You have at least 5 years- relevant professional experience in international contract law or research management - ideally gained in an international organisation, a company in the tech/space sector, a space-related authority or at a university. Experience with contracts from space agencies (e.g. ESA) or space companies is a strong advantage.
* **Expertise:** You have in-depth knowledge of Swiss and international contract law. Experience in intellectual property law, technology transfer or research law is an advantage.
* **Space law**: Knowledge of international space law, regulatory issues relating to the space sector, and the science policy context of international research collaborations would be an advantage.
* **Export control & regulation:** Experience in export control law (particularly ITAR/EAR), in dealing with dual-use goods or in comparable regulatory environments is particularly welcome. Knowledge of ESA or NASA-related regulatory frameworks is an additional advantage.
* **Skills:** You possess excellent analytical and conceptual skills, strong negotiation skills, and the ability to address legal risks in a pragmatic and solution-oriented manner.
* **Languages:** You communicate and negotiate fluently in German and English (both spoken and written). Business-level English is essential.
* **Mindset & working style:** You are characterised by a strong service orientation and a pragmatic, solution-oriented approach to your work. You are a talented communicator and are confident in your interactions with researchers, industry representatives and regulatory authorities.
By drafting clear and balanced contractual provisions, you lay the foundations for successful international collaborations. You can manage a demanding portfolio independently and conduct complex contract negotiations efficiently and in a goal-oriented manner.
If, in addition, you have an interest in the space sector, cutting-edge technology and international research collaborations, and are passionate about scientific innovation, you are ideally suited for this role.

Job description
En tant que membre du département juridique du Swatch Group, vous vous occupez des affaires légales de certaines de nos sociétés marques et filiales du Groupe à l'étranger.

Dans cette position, vous conseillez au quotidien les différents départements des entreprises, de la production et marketing aux ventes en passant par le service après\-vente, les ressources humaines, l'approvisionnement, les finances et la IT dans des questions juridiques des plus variées.

Vous contribuez à réaliser de grands projets au niveau international, que ce soit l'introduction de nouveaux produits, le développement des ventes en ligne ou de nouvelles solutions informatiques.
Vous conseillez et soutenez nos sociétés marques et nos filiales du Groupe à l'étranger dans les questions relatives à leur réseau de distribution, y compris du point de vue du droit de la concurrence, et préparez les contrats y afférant.

Vous examinez les questions de droit de propriété intellectuelle relatives au design de montres et aux campagnes publicitaires et rédigez divers contrats. Vous traitez les questions de droit du travail et négociez les contrats de bails pour les boutiques en Suisse.

Vous gérez les éventuelles procédures judiciaires vous\-même ou en collaboration avec des avocats externes,. Vous assurez le respect des lignes directrices du Groupe dans les différents domaines d'activité. Enfin, vous échangez avec vos collègues des filiales du Groupe à l'étranger pour coordonner les aspects légaux de grands projets.
De manière générale, vous utilisez vos excellentes connaissances juridiques et votre expérience pour examiner, analyser, rédiger et négocier efficacement des contrats dans un large éventail de domaines juridiques, élaborer de manière indépendante des propositions de solutions et évaluer correctement les conséquences juridiques et économiques.
Vous jouez un rôle important au sein d'une équipe de juristes motivés et doués.
Profile
Vous connaissez très bien le droit suisse et êtes titulaire d'un brevet d'avocat ou d'une autre formation équivalente et possédez une expérience professionnelle de plusieurs années en entreprise ou dans un cabinet de droit commercial.

Vous êtes familier avec les projets commerciaux à ampleur internationale et vous sentez à l'aise pour négocier des contrats complexes avec des interlocuteurs à l'étranger.
Languages
De langue maternelle française ou allemande avec des très bonnes connaissances dans l'autre langue, vous avez l'habitude de travailler en français, anglais et allemand.

Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.
We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.
The Principal Product & Commercial Counsel will report to Docker's Head of Legal. This is a hybrid role at the intersection of product counseling and commercial negotiation.

You will serve as the primary legal partner to Docker's Product Management and Engineering teams across the full product lifecycle, from concept and design through launch, monetization, and end of life, while also assisting with negotiating the commercial provisions that bring those products to market.

Your subject matter depth in open source software licensing and cloud services will directly impact how Docker builds, licenses, and delivers its products to millions of developers and thousands of enterprise customers worldwide.
Your work will be instrumental in helping the Company reach its growth objectives while protecting its intellectual property and managing product and licensing risk. This position will be a core member of the extended Legal team, working cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, GRC, Sales, and Deal Desk, with exposure to Docker's senior executives and the opportunity to grow beyond the initial responsibilities and role based on expanding company needs.

Primary function will be to serve as embedded product counsel to Docker's Product Managers and Engineering teams, providing pragmatic, business-oriented advice on new products, features, pricing and packaging changes, Early Access and beta programs, and end-of-life decisions.
Advise on open source software matters, including license analysis and compatibility (Apache, MIT, BSD, GPL, LGPL, AGPL, and source-available licenses), inbound and outbound OSS usage, contribution and CLA policies, and compliance obligations across Docker's products and distribution channels.
Secondary function as needed, draft and maintain Docker's product-facing legal terms, including service-specific terms, subscription and licensing agreements, Early Access and beta terms, fair use and acceptable use policies, and documentation supporting new monetization models.
Structure and negotiate commercial provisions in customer and partner agreements relating to product licensing, cloud services, hybrid on-premise and SaaS deployments, IP ownership, indemnification, warranties, and support commitments, in partnership with Sales and Deal Desk.
Counsel on AI-enabled product features, including training data provenance, output ownership, third-party model licensing, and evolving AI regulatory requirements.
Collaborate with GRC on the intersection of product design and regulatory obligations, including software supply chain security expectations and emerging regimes such as the EU Cyber Resilience Act.
Support IP strategy, including trademark usage guidelines, brand protection in product and marketing contexts, and coordination with outside counsel on IP matters.
Monitor and analyze legal and regulatory developments affecting developer tools, open source, cloud services, and AI, advising the organization on necessary updates and adjustments.
Help build scalable playbooks, templates, and self-service resources that allow Product and GTM teams to move quickly within well-defined guardrails.

J.D. from an accredited law school and active membership in good standing in at least one U.S. state bar.
6+ years of relevant legal experience, with a meaningful portion in-house at a software, cloud, or developer tools company; a combination of law firm and in-house experience is ideal.
Deep familiarity with open source software licensing, including copyleft and permissive license regimes, license compatibility analysis, and OSS program governance.
Hands-on experience drafting and negotiating SaaS, software licensing, and cloud services agreements, including enterprise customer negotiations of IP, indemnity, and liability provisions.
Working technical fluency with developer software concepts such as virtual containers, registries, CI/CD, APIs, and software supply chain security; direct familiarity with Docker's products or comparable developer platforms is a strong plus.
Understanding of AI and LLM legal issues, including model licensing, training data, and applicable regulatory frameworks such as the EU AI Act.
AI-Native work capability.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex legal concepts into clear, actionable guidance for Product Managers and Engineers.
Sound, risk-calibrated judgment and a bias toward practical solutions that enable the business.
Proven ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment and to manage competing priorities independently.
Ability to collaborate with diverse teams and build strong working relationships.
What to expect
First 30 days
Meet with the Head of Legal to understand Docker's product, licensing, and IP vision.
Read Docker's product terms, subscription agreements, and OSS policies.
Read Docker's Legal, Products, and security-related Notion pages.
Become familiar with Docker's product portfolio, licensing models, and distribution channels.
Forge relationships with Docker's Product Management, Engineering, GRC, Deal Desk, and Sales teams.
Begin reviewing product feature launches and customer requests for product-related commercial terms.
First 90 days
Take ownership of the legal review process for new product and feature launches.
Establish a formalized intake and review cadence with Product Management for roadmap items with legal implications.
Deliver a fact and data driven assessment of Docker's product terms and OSS compliance posture with a 6 month and 12 month improvement roadmap.
Lead the negotiation of product and licensing provisions in active customer and partner deals as assigned by the Head of Legal.
Collaborate with Docker counsel on customer contractual requests relating to licensing, IP, and cloud services and provide feedback.
Become familiar with Docker's Compliance program and controls.
First year
You have maintained an appropriate meeting cadence with Docker's Product Management, Engineering, GRC, Deal Desk, and Sales teams.
You have provided a monthly update report to the Head of Legal for eStaff updates.
You have built and deployed playbooks and templates that streamline product legal review and commercial negotiations to meet the demands of domestic and international growth.
You have built the brand of the product legal function as a trusted partner, industry leader, and facilitator of Docker's growth and customer satisfaction.

Satispay began by rethinking the simple act of a payment to remove the friction from our daily routines. But we didn't stop there. Today, we are building a complete financial platform designed to empower people and concretely improve their lives.
By giving our 6 million users a clear, open path to pay, save, and invest, we are evolving into the definitive destination for every financial need.
What you'll be doing
As our Legal Counsel, your focus will be on providing high-level legal guidance within the dynamic Fintech sector, particularly in payments, e-money, and consumer credit products. You will offer strategic counsel on regulatory, contractual, and product-related matters to ensure compliance and mitigate risks. Here's what your day-to-day will look like:
Product development support – Collaborate cross-functionally to design and launch new products and services in Payments and Consumer Credit (such as BNPL), integrating basic technical and engineering considerations into legal analysis.
Risk assessment & management – Identify legal and regulatory risks, proposing effective mitigation strategies aligned with our risk appetite to safeguard the organization.
Regulatory compliance – Advise on relevant financial regulatory requirements, including PSD2, AML/KYC, e-money regulations, and CCD2, ensuring adherence.
Stakeholder management – Act as a trusted advisor to senior leadership, providing pragmatic legal guidance and fostering a culture of legal awareness across the organization.

We need a problem-solver who loves teamwork and gets things done. If you're curious and ready for real ownership, you'll fit in!
Does this sound like you?
Relevant education – Qualified lawyer with a minimum of 5 years PQE, and ideally 8–10 years of professional legal experience.
Relevant technical and regulatory knowledge – Deep knowledge of financial and consumer credit regulations (PSD2, AML/KYC, EMRs, CCD2) and a demonstrable track record in Fintech and Payments, ideally with experience in both private practice and in-house settings.
Analytical mindset – Ability to dive deep into complex legal issues, exercise strong judgment, and make sound risk-based decisions.
Technical and commercial awareness – Clear understanding of basic technology and engineering processes in Fintech, Payments, and consumer lending, with prior experience working with technical teams being a significant plus; ability to balance legal risks with commercial considerations.
Language fluency – English fluency (both written and spoken) is essential, while knowledge of Italian or French is a plus for effective communication within our international context.

Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join
Airbnb’s Legal team embodies the company’s innovative, forward-thinking spirit. At the frontier of the new sharing economy, Airbnb is breaking new ground in matters of policy, law, and government relations. Where some see obstacles, we see the opportunity to find creative, practical solutions, right at the cutting edge.

Our adventurous, fast-moving legal team is committed to building a team of talented, collaborative and self-motivated legal professionals across the globe who believe in Airbnb’s mission and leading as a 21st century company.
The Difference You Will Make
We are looking for an experienced, highly motivated attorney to join us as Lead Counsel, Community Trust to provide legal support and counseling on fraud and safety defenses and enforcement, community support, law enforcement operations, global crisis management and disaster response. These are some of the most important issues we work on in the Legal department and your work will play a critical role. The position reports to our Associate General Counsel, Community Trust.
This is a unique opportunity to work on novel issues in an exciting, fast-paced environment. This job is for you if you have superb analytical skills, enjoy ambiguity, love working on complex legal, policy and social issues, and believe that a company can change the world by encouraging immersive travel and experiences.

You must work well with business partners as well as lawyers, have an upbeat positive attitude even in the face of crisis, thrive on building relationships and collaborating with cross-functional partners throughout the company.
A Typical Day
Support the Fraud & Safety Operations team in proactive defenses and reactive interventions to help keep our community safe
Support on user Customer Support escalations, including analysis, and advice on an array of matters that implicate Airbnb policies and policy enforcement
Assess, manage, and provide legal advice to cross-functional stakeholders regarding global legal risks, life safety and law enforcement operations, and related internal investigations
Ability to both advise on and drive cross-functional projects with business partners, including Fraud & Safety, Global Crisis Management, Community Support, Communications, Community Policy, Public Policy, Privacy, and Hosting teams.
Help manage team resources to align with business priorities and objectives
Active championship of Airbnb’s mission, ethics and integrity
Support of Airbnb’s commitment to building and maintaining a diverse and inclusive workplace, free of discrimination and harassment
Your Expertise
J.D. with strong academic credentials and demonstrated record of success as a senior in-house lawyer, law firm partner, or commensurate federal or state government position.
Member of California Bar or eligible to register as Registered In-House Counsel
12 - 15 years of significant knowledge and experience with issues such as litigation, risk mitigation, fraud and safety, law enforcement operations, global policy application. Experience with artificial intelligence and machine learning models is a plus.
Outstanding analytical, oral, and writing skills, including the ability to distill complex legal issues efficiently and effectively for a business audience, often in novel or ambiguous situations
Possess a highly-developed sense of urgency in time sensitive and high stakes matters
Demonstrated record of entrepreneurial, quick-thinking, pragmatic, business-oriented advice that properly balances both legal risk and business reward
Highly motivated, ability to take ownership of a project from inception to completion, efficient, and organized with proven ability to thrive in a fast-paced work environment
Excellent communication skills with capacity to advocate for a position while maintaining respectful, collaborative and open-minded approach
Ability to lead with humility and empathy
Passion for travel, home sharing and deep appreciation for Airbnb community
Good sense of humor, disdain for drama, and desire to get things done

By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly.

Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.
Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.
Legal at Brex
The Legal team helps the company grow responsibly, advocating for Brex and for the thousands of growing businesses we serve. We provide strategic advice and guidance to all Brex teams, protect Brex, advise on risk, and represent the company externally, negotiating with partners and interacting with regulators. Reimagining the financial system in a highly regulated environment requires creativity and resourcefulness, and we welcome the challenge.

As Commercial Counsel at Brex, you will be an integral and versatile member of the Legal team and will support all aspects of the Company's commercial legal efforts.

You will handle legal review and negotiation of Brex customer contracts, working closely with sales and other revenue-supporting teams to close deals efficiently while protecting the Company's interests. You'll also support vendor and partner contracting, negotiating a range of contracts that serve teams and departments across Brex.

You will advise on legal issues that intersect with commercial matters, and collaborate with a wide range of cross-functional partners, including deal desk, ops, procurement, privacy, security, marketing, and people.

You will contribute to the development and implementation of commercial legal resources and processes, including internal policies and procedures and contracting workflows. You'll provide sound and pragmatic legal advice and take a business-oriented approach to problem solving!

Draft, review, and negotiate customer agreements, from initial legal review through final signature, in partnership with sales, deal desk, and other stakeholders.
Support the legal review and negotiation of a wide variety of inbound commercial contracts, including AI, SaaS, and other technology agreements, master and professional services agreements, consulting agreements, marketing, agency, and media contracts, event agreements, and non-disclosure agreements.
Drive continuous improvement in commercial contracting processes, including developing and refining contracting playbooks, internal policies and procedures, and leveraging and optimizing AI contracting tools and contract lifecycle management (CLM) workflows.
Identify and mitigate contractual risks within established parameters, escalating complex issues to SMEs and senior legal team members as needed.
Provide sound, business-oriented legal advice to cross-functional partners on contract terms, deal structures, and commercial legal risks and opportunities.
Collaborate closely with internal stakeholders to understand business needs, contextualize transactions, and translate business, operational and product requirements into clear legal terms and conditions.
Be a business partner, not just an attorney!

Entrepreneurial mindset and comfort with taking ownership and acting upon it; you welcome challenges and thrive in dynamic, fast-paced environments!
Minimum of 3-5 years of relevant experience practicing commercial law, either in-house at a technology company or within the corporate/tech transactions department of a reputable law firm. Experience at fast-paced growing technology companies is preferred.
Juris Doctor (JD) and active bar membership in good standing in at least one US jurisdiction.
Demonstrated experience drafting, reviewing, and negotiating complex technology and commercial contracts; experience with both customer-facing and vendor/inbound contracting is ideal.
Exceptional judgment, attention to detail, and integrity, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
You are a builder, motivated by the continuous development and improvement of internal processes and resources.
Flexible, adaptive, and always open to learning something new.

Fintech or financial services experience, or familiarity with fintech product structures.
Working knowledge of privacy issues in a commercial context.
Experience working directly with a deal desk team.
